html:
SMTO-SKL-0065 — SMTO couldn't find that calendar or meeting

GUID: a0a47c46-0e08-5ab6-b274-a78970852281
Slug: microsoft365-calendar-event-not-found
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • The meeting or calendar SMTO was asked to use isn't there for this Microsoft 365 account. It may have been deleted or moved, or it belongs to a different account.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to list your meetings for that day, for example "show my meetings on Friday", and check that the meeting is there. This gets the meeting's current details, which change if it was moved, recreated or deleted.
  2. Open your Outlook calendar and check whether the meeting still exists; if you were deleting or cancelling it, it may already be gone. If the meeting is already gone, there is nothing left to do and you shouldn't ask again.
  3. If you have more than one Microsoft account, type @ and pick the account that owns this calendar, then ask again. A meeting in one account can't be found from another account.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows or updates the meeting you meant, and Outlook shows the same result.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to change a different meeting that only looks similar.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Microsoft Graph returned resource-not-found during a Microsoft 365 calendar operation, so the event or calendar ID did not resolve for the selected account.

What this means

  • A resource-not-found response during a calendar-prefixed operation is translated into the calendar-event-not-found family. This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • A resource-not-found response during a calendar-prefixed operation is translated into the calendar-event-not-found family.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact failing calendar route and resource ID; the family label does not prove an event was deleted.

How to fix it

  • Re-read the calendar under the same account_ref (calendars or calendar_events for the relevant window) and use the exact current event_id and calendar_id; do not substitute an event from another account or tenant. If a delete or cancel was the original request, confirm whether the event is already gone before issuing anything else.
  • Read the exact calendar resource under the same account and resolve its current ID or access without guessing another event.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • An authorized same-account read identifies the intended calendar resource.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
